title: Perfect approximations to pseudo-coherent complexes on qcqs algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$, with its small etale structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose that its point space is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover) and its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A perfect object is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be pseudo-coherent, meaning that etale locally on affine scheme charts it is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free structure modules. Then $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, and for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ there are $P,C\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and a distinguished triangle $P\xrightarrow{u}E\to C\to P[1]$ such that $P$ is perfect, $H^i(u)$ is an isomorphism for every $i>a$, and $H^a(u)$ is surjective. No Noetherian, separatedness, finite-type or base-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08HP, theorem-approximation, with T=X in Tags 08HI (definition-approximation-holds) and 08HJ (definition-approximation); Tag 08JL, lemma-pseudo-coherent, for quasi-coherent cohomology.

proof.text: First check quasi-coherence. On the affine etale charts in the hypothesis, represent $E$ by the indicated bounded-above finite free complex. Finite free structure modules have the identity local presentation, hence are quasi-coherent. Kernels, images and cokernels of maps between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent, so each cohomology of this complex is quasi-coherent. The etale chart criterion therefore gives $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. The same argument applies to every perfect object: a direct summand of a finite free module is the image of its idempotent endomorphism, so its terms and cohomologies are quasi-coherent. Moreover $E$ is $b$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $b$: brutally truncate each finite free model below $b$. The resulting bounded finite free complex maps to the model, agrees on cohomology above $b$, and surjects in degree $b$ because it omits only the incoming boundaries.

source.place: Tag 08JL (lemma-pseudo-coherent), local-complex argument; Tag 08HI and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FT.

proof.text: For a qcqs etale object $Y\to X$, use the property $\mathsf A(Y)$. Its affine base case follows from the existing scheme affine theorem. Indeed, if $Y$ is an affine scheme and $T$ has quasi-compact complement, choose the integer $r$ supplied by the scheme property $\mathsf A(Y)$. Given an admissible small-etale $F$, write $F\cong\epsilon_Y^*F_0$ under the derived quasi-coherent equivalence. Etale detection of pseudo-coherence makes $F_0$ $(m-r)$-pseudo-coherent. Support outside $T$ is preserved and reflected: restrict the pullback comparison to any open in the complement, where the exact faithful functor $\epsilon^*$ preserves and reflects zero cohomology. Apply the scheme property with this same $r$ to get $P_0\to F_0$. Exact pullback gives $\epsilon_Y^*P_0\to F$ with the required cohomology maps; etale detection of perfectness and the same restriction comparison give perfectness and support. Thus $\mathsf A(Y)$ holds, including the empty affine scheme.

source.place: Tag 08HM (lemma-approximation-affine), comparison with perfect.tex Tag 08EQ and Tags 08EM/08EN; Tags 071Q, 08HE, 08HG.

proof.text: Apply the qcqs distinguished-square induction principle to this property. In a square $(U\subset W,V\to W)$ quantified over there, $W$ is qcqs, $U$ is quasi-compact, $V$ is affine, and the overlap is qcqs and hence quasi-compact, as part of the induction theorem's domain assertion. The supported approximation square-step theorem therefore applies to $\mathsf A(U)$ and gives $\mathsf A(W)$; the induction hypotheses on $V$ and the overlap need not be used. The affine case just proved supplies the other premise. The induction principle yields $\mathsf A(X)$.

In $\mathsf A(X)$ choose $T=|X|$, whose complement is empty and whose open immersion is quasi-compact. Let $r$ be its witness and set $m=a$. Step 1 gives $(a-r)$-pseudo-coherence of $E$ and membership in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$; the support hypothesis outside $T$ is vacuous. The defining conclusion gives a perfect $P$ and $u:P\to E$ inducing isomorphisms for $i>a$ and a surjection for $i=a$. The quasi-coherence argument of step 1 also gives $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$.

source.place: Tags 08HI, 08HJ: specialization of approximation to full support.

proof.text: Complete $u$ to a distinguished triangle $P\to E\to C\to P[1]$ in the module derived category, using its triangulated structure and TR1. The cohomology long exact sequence expresses $H^i(C)$ as an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(H^i(P)\to H^i(E))$ by $\ker(H^{i+1}(P)\to H^{i+1}(E))$. Both ends are quasi-coherent by kernel/cokernel closure, and extension closure gives quasi-coherence of the middle. Thus $C\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, and the full subcategory contains the displayed triangle. This argument applies for every integer $a$ and introduces none of the excluded geometric hypotheses.
